record.original_question: Study the various possible notions of relative irregularity for families of higher-dimensional varieties, under appropriate conditions on the fibres.

evidence.quote: Problem 2 (Rita Pardini) Study the various possible notions of relative irregularity for fam￾ilies of higher-dimensional varieties (with appropriate conditions on the fibres).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a fibration $f\colon X \to B$ from a smooth complex projective surface $X$ onto a smooth projective curve $B$, the relative irregularity is classically defined as $q_f := h^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X) - g(B)$, where $g(B)$ is the genus of $B$. This invariant plays a central role in the geometry of surface fibrations (e.g., in Xiao's conjecture and the Severi inequality).

Investigate analogous notions of relative irregularity for families $f\colon X \to B$ of higher-dimensional smooth projective varieties (i.e., where the general fibre $F$ has $\dim F \geq 2$), under suitable hypotheses on the fibres (for instance, fibres of general type, fibres of maximal Albanese dimension, or fibres with prescribed Hodge-theoretic properties). Formulate the possible definitions of relative irregularity in this higher-dimensional setting, compare them, establish their basic properties, and determine the inequalities or geometric constraints (analogous to those known in the surface case) that they must satisfy.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Rita Pardini in 2018, asks for a systematic study rather than a single yes/no answer, so it is open-ended by nature. Related progress exists (e.g., a relative Severi inequality for fibrations of maximal Albanese dimension over curves has been established), but the broader programme of defining and studying various notions of relative irregularity for higher-dimensional families remains an active and incomplete area of research.

status_evidence.title: Open problems (Pardini's Problem 2)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 2 (Rita Pardini): Study the various possible notions of relative irregularity for families of higher-dimensional varieties (with appropriate conditions on the fibres).

status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for specific classes of higher-dimensional fibrations but does not close the general programme.
